Природный апокалипсис: на Шахты обрушился град размером с грецкий орех
Город Шахты днем 19 июня попал под влияние стихии. Около 13:30 пошел ливень, к которому быстро добавился град. Льдинки размером с грецкий орех начали лупить по окнам, припаркованным машинам, домам и земле. При этом ливень усилился и по улицам потекли бурные реки вперемешку со льдом.
Длился природный апокалипсис в течение 20 минут. Затем град прекратился, но продолжился дождь.
Так как стихия сопровождалась сильным ветром, произошел обрыв проводов электричества и интернета. С деревьев облетели листья, поломало сухие ветки.

On the afternoon of June 19, the city of Shakhty was hit by a natural disaster. Around 1:30 p.m., a downpour began, quickly followed by hail. Hailstones the size of walnuts began pelting windows, parked cars, houses, and the ground. Editorial Standards

fact_alert.original_text:
Heavy thunderstorms hit Vermont on Thursday, triggering a flash flood warning for part of Bennington County and causing power outages across the state.
Storms began rolling over the state early Thursday morning, and by the afternoon, the National Weather Service had issued severe thunderstorm warnings for the area around Rutland, Middlebury, Montpelier and much of Windsor County. Warnings for high winds and tornadoes were also issued for much of the state.
“We definitely are seeing several parts of power outages, trees down, power lines down, those are the main impacts of this line of storm,” said Adrianna Kremer, a meteorologist in the Burlington office of the National Weather Service.
As of 4 p.m., high winds and heavy rain had left more than 20,000 customers without power, mostly in Windsor and Bennington counties.
WCAX and NBC5 reported a possible tornado around Woodstock.
“We have outages in all of our districts, so we have about 15 district offices around the state, and the hardest hit are in Sunderland, White River, Montpelier and Royalton districts,” said Kristin Carlson, a spokesperson for Green Mountain Power.
Carlson said that crews had already restored power to 10,000 customers by late afternoon, but it was too early to give an estimate as to when power would be restored to those still without it.
A flash flood warning was issued in Dorset and Sandgate in Bennington County, with an inch and a half of rain rapidly dropping on the region, according to Kremer. The warning is in effect until 6 p.m.
The line of storms was set to pass over Vermont by the end of Thursday, according to the weather service.
“Luckily the main impacts are slowly moving out of Vermont in the next hour or so, so it should be improving here on out,” Kremer said. “But definitely just encourage people to stay weather-aware and be safe today.”
Storms and prolonged rain are expected throughout the weekend starting Friday night, with the possibility of more thunderstorms, according to the weather service.
fact_alert.caption: Flash flood warning issued in Dorset and Sandgate areas of Bennington County with 20,000 customers experiencing power outages in Windsor and Bennington counties, VT: Blog.

Как сообщил в Telegram-канале депутат Госдумы Иван Демченко, от паводка пострадали порядка 30 местных сельхозпроизводителей. Фото: пресс-служба администрации Крымского района
Основной удар стихии пришелся на район хутора Западного в Троицком сельском поселении — сейчас ведется работа по устранению прорыва дамбы. Напомним, что режим чрезвычайной ситуации был введен ранее в Крымском и Славянском районах. По данным оперштаба на 16 июня, уровень воды в реках уже опустился ниже опасных отметок, однако вода продолжает поступать на сельхозземли.

دير الزور-سانا
وزّعت إدارة الإغاثة الطارئة في وزارة الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث، 2340 سلة غذائية على العائلات المتضررة من ارتفاع منسوب نهر الفرات في عدد من مناطق ريف دير الزور، وذلك ضمن المساعدات الإماراتية المقدّمة لدعم المتضررين.
وذكرت الوزارة عبر قناتها على تلغرام، أن الدفعة الأولى من المساعدات البالغ عددها 8500 سلة غذائية، تشمل مناطق المريعية، وحطلة، وجيدة بكارة، والصبحة، والدحلة، ومظلوم، ومراط، وجديدة عكيدات، وطابية جزيرة، والطيانة، وشنان، والجمة.
وأشارت الوزارة إلى أن هذه المساعدات التي تأتي في إطار الاستجابة الطارئة للمتضررين من ارتفاع منسوب نهر الفرات، ستستمر خلال الفترة المقبلة في محافظة دير الزور، على أن تشمل العائلات المتضررة في محافظة الرقة أيضاً، بما يضمن توسيع نطاق الاستجابة وتعزيز وصول المساعدات إلى مستحقيها، وتخفيف الأعباء المعيشية عن الأسر المتضررة وضمان تلبية احتياجاتها الغذائية الأساسية.
وعملت فرق وزارة الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث، على تنفيذ تدخلاتها الميدانية في محافظتي دير الزور والرقة، على خلفية ارتفاع منسوب مياه نهر الفرات، ضمن غرفة طوارئ مشتركة تضم الجهات المعنية، بهدف الحد من الأضرار وضمان سلامة المدنيين واستمرارية عمل المنشآت الحيوية.

fact_alert.translated_text:
Deir ez-Zor—SANA
The Emergency Relief Directorate at the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management distributed 2,340 food baskets to families affected by the rising waters of the Euphrates River in a number of rural areas of Deir ez-Zor, as part of the aid provided by the United Arab Emirates to support those affected.
The ministry stated via its Telegram channel that the first batch of aid, consisting of 8,500 food baskets, covers the areas of Al-Muraiya, Hatla, Jida Bakara, Al-Sabha, Al-Dahla, Mazlum, Marat, Jida Akidat, Tabiya Jazira, Al-Tayana, Shannan, and Al-Jama.
The ministry noted that this aid, which is part of the emergency response for those affected by the rising waters of the Euphrates River, will continue in the coming period in Deir ez-Zor Governorate and will also include affected families in Raqqa Governorate, thereby ensuring that the scope of the response is expanded and that aid reaches those who are entitled to it, alleviating the financial burdens on affected families and ensuring that their basic food needs are met.
Teams from the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management carried out field operations in the governorates of Deir ez-Zor and Raqqa in response to rising water levels in the Euphrates River, as part of a joint emergency response center comprising relevant agencies, with the aim of minimizing damage, ensuring the safety of civilians, and maintaining the operation of critical infrastructure.

fact_alert.original_text:
Severe weather and flooding threat continue into Friday
MERIDIAN, Miss. (WTOK) - After a total washout for most of Thursday, we’ll see another round of rain and severe weather possible heading into Friday before it’s all said and done.
FIRST ALERT: LOW END SEVERE, SIGNIFICANT FLOODING RISK FOR FRIDAY
The Storm Prediction Center has our whole area under a Marginal (1/5) threat for severe weather heading into Friday, with some storms capable of producing strong gusty winds that could cause damage, but that is not the top priority issue for Friday. The southern part of our area is under a Significant (3/4) threat for excessive rainfall and flash flooding heading into Friday, with the other part of our area under a Slight (2/4) risk for flooding. We could see up to another 1 to 2 inches of rainfall, on top of the 2 to 3 inches we saw over the course of the day on Thursday. A flood watch will also remain in effect until Friday evening. Make sure to stay tuned to your First Alert Weather Team for updates on these threats.
Beyond the threat for flooding and the minor severe threat, temperatures over the next few days remain pleasant, if not a bit summer-like. Highs remain in the mid and upper 80s through the back part of our week, with heavy rain and some thunderstorms over Friday, then scattered showers and storms over Saturday and Sunday.
We’ll return to the lower 90s heading into the coming workweek, with more afternoon chances for scattered showers and storms.
TRACKING THE TROPICS
There is one area to watch in the coming days, as the remnants of Tropical Storm Arthur move across the southeastern U.S. and back off the East Coast, where favorable waters could bring about another system with the disturbance. There is a 10% chance of development over the next 24 hours, and 10% over the next 7 days. Stay tuned for updates.

В Крымском районе после прорыва дамбы затопило 11 тысяч гектаров
В Крымском районе Краснодарского края сохраняется сложная паводковая ситуация после прорыва дамбы в районе хутора Западного Троицкого сельского поселения. Общая площадь подтопленных территорий превысила 11 тыс. га. Об этом сообщил депутат Государственной думы Иван Демченко, прибывший в муниципалитет.
Фото: пресс-служба администрации Крымского района
По его словам, свыше 6 тыс. га затопленной территории составляют сельскохозяйственные угодья. Последствия паводка затронули около 30 аграрных предприятий. В Крымском и Славянском районах после повреждения гидротехнических сооружений под водой оказались порядка 6 тыс. га полей.
Основные силы сейчас направили на ликвидацию прорана в теле дамбы. Работы ведут в районе хутора Западного круглосуточно в несколько смен. Для восстановления поврежденного участка привлекли технику и специалистов Абинского электрометаллургического завода.
В муниципалитете продолжают укреплять дамбу и откачивать воду с подтопленных территорий. Власти и экстренные службы контролируют ситуацию в районах, где сохраняется угроза дальнейшего подъема воды.
Ранее в Крымском районе сообщали о подготовке к возможной эвакуации жителей нескольких населенных пунктов из-за риска подтопления. В муниципалитете действует режим чрезвычайной ситуации. Аналогичный режим ранее ввели и в Славянском районе.
По данным местных властей, сильные осадки и повреждение дамб привели к затоплению сельхозземель и гибели части посевов. Ущерб продолжают оценивать специалисты. Одновременно с аварийно-восстановительными работами в районах организовали мониторинг состояния гидротехнических сооружений и уровня воды.
Синоптики ранее предупреждали, что в Краснодарском крае сохраняется неблагоприятная погодная обстановка. В регионе прогнозируют сильные осадки, грозы и усиление ветра.

Most of the resources are currently being directed toward repairing the breach in the dam. Work is being carried out around the clock in several shifts in the area near the village of Zapadnoye. Equipment and specialists from the Abinsk Electrometallurgical Plant were brought in to repair the damaged section.
The municipality continues to reinforce the levee and pump water out of the flooded areas. Authorities and emergency services are monitoring the situation in areas where there is still a risk of further rising water levels.

According to local authorities, heavy rainfall and damage to dams led to the flooding of farmland and the loss of some crops. Experts are still assessing the damage. Le ministère de l’Agriculture, des Ressources hydrauliques et de la Pêche maritime a assuré que la situation dans la zone de l’oued Mellègue est totalement sous contrôle, à la suite d’un incident technique survenu à Sakoura ayant provoqué une hausse temporaire du niveau des eaux et leur écoulement vers l’oued Medjerda.
Selon les autorités, cet épisode n’a entraîné aucun danger pour les populations riveraines ni pour leurs habitations. Le ministère précise également que la circulation sur les routes nationales et régionales reste normale et sans perturbation, tandis que le cours de l’oued Medjerda est en mesure d’absorber les volumes d’eau transférés vers le barrage de Sidi Salem.
Dans le cadre du suivi de la situation, le secrétaire d’État auprès du ministre de l’Agriculture chargé des ressources en eau s’est rendu sur place dans la soirée de mardi, accompagné du directeur général des barrages et des grands travaux hydrauliques ainsi que d’une équipe d’ingénieurs et d’experts. Une inspection a été effectuée afin de vérifier la sécurité des infrastructures et de suivre l’évolution du débit.
Les constatations techniques ont confirmé que la stabilité de l’ouvrage hydraulique n’est pas compromise et qu’aucun impact n’est enregistré sur la sécurité des citoyens. Les autorités indiquent également qu’aucune perte significative d’eau n’a été constatée, l’ensemble des volumes étant acheminé normalement vers le barrage de Sidi Salem.
Le ministère souligne par ailleurs que le débit des eaux est en baisse progressive par rapport aux premières heures de l’incident et que la résolution complète du problème technique est attendue dans la soirée.
Les services centraux et régionaux poursuivent un suivi permanent de la situation 24 heures sur 24, avec des équipes déployées le long de l’oued afin de surveiller l’évolution et d’évaluer d’éventuels impacts sur les terres agricoles. Les commissions régionales et centrales restent également en veille permanente pour prendre les mesures nécessaires si besoin.
Enfin, le ministère appelle les citoyens à s’informer uniquement auprès des sources officielles et affirme qu’il continuera de communiquer régulièrement sur l’évolution de la situation.
S.R

The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Marine Fisheries has assured the public that the situation in the Mellègue wadi area is fully under control, following a technical incident in Sakoura that caused a temporary rise in water levels and their flow into the Medjerda wadi.
According to the authorities, this incident posed no danger to residents living along the riverbanks or to their homes. The ministry also stated that traffic on national and regional roads remains normal and uninterrupted, while the Medjerda River is capable of absorbing the volume of water diverted to the Sidi Salem Dam.
As part of efforts to monitor the situation, the Secretary of State to the Minister of Agriculture in charge of water resources visited the site on Tuesday evening, accompanied by the Director General of Dams and Major Hydraulic Works, as well as a team of engineers and experts. An inspection was conducted to verify the safety of the infrastructure and monitor changes in flow rates.
Technical findings confirmed that the stability of the hydraulic structure is not compromised and that there is no impact on public safety. Authorities also indicate that no significant water loss has been observed, with all water volumes being channeled normally to the Sidi Salem Dam.
The ministry further emphasizes that the water flow is gradually decreasing compared to the early hours of the incident and that the technical issue is expected to be fully resolved by this evening.
Central and regional agencies are continuously monitoring the situation 24 hours a day, with teams deployed along the wadi to track developments and assess any potential impacts on farmland. Regional and central commissions also remain on constant standby to take the necessary measures if needed.
Finally, the ministry urges citizens to rely solely on official sources for information and affirms that it will continue to provide regular updates on the situation.
S.R

FIRST ALERT WEATHER DAY: Heavy rain, flooding, isolated tornadoes and gusty winds all expected today
Tropical Low Brings Dangerous Weather to North Georgia
ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — What’s left of Tropical Storm Arthur will bring dangerous weather to north Georgia today, prompting us to declare a First Alert Weather Day.
Heavy rain, gusty winds and the potential for isolated tornadoes are expected as what remains of the tropical system tracks through the area. Flooding poses the greatest threat, particularly this evening and tonight.
When the storms arrive
Scattered storms will develop after lunch Thursday in north Georgia, with conditions intensifying as the day progresses. The heaviest rain will move into north Georgia from the west between 5 and 6 p.m., continuing throughout the night before moving out by 2 a.m. Friday morning.
The timing coincides with the evening commute, making travel potentially hazardous during peak hours.
Active alerts in effect
A flood watch is in effect from metro Atlanta southward through Friday morning, with the highest risk of flooding expected this evening and tonight.
A wind advisory is also in effect for the same areas during the same timeframe.
Residents in flood-prone areas should prepare for the possibility of water rising quickly in creeks, streams and poor drainage areas.
What to expect
Flooding: The primary threat Thursday evening and overnight. Even small streams and normally dry areas could see water rise rapidly.
Isolated tornadoes: A tornado threat exists along and south of I-20 this afternoon and evening. While isolated, tornadoes are possible with the strongest storms.
Gusty winds: Wind gusts up to 35 mph are expected, especially this evening. Secure loose outdoor items and be prepared for minor wind damage.
What You Should Do
- Avoid driving through flooded roadways — turn around, don’t drown.
- Bring pets and outdoor items indoors.
- Charge your phone and have flashlights and batteries ready.
- Monitor weather updates frequently.
- Stay away from windows during severe storms.
- If a tornado warning is issued for your area, move to an interior room on the lowest level of a sturdy building.
Looking Ahead
Saturday will bring a break in the weather with dry conditions expected. However, rain will return to north Georgia on Father’s Day Sunday.

The system is expected to continue weakening as it moves east over land at 15 mph, but it could emerge of the East Coast by Friday, the NHC said.
Conditions in the Atlantic could be marginally conducive for some subtropical or tropical development Friday or Saturday.
As of 7 a.m. Thursday, Arthur’s remnants have about a 10% chance of development over the next 48 hours and seven days.
Regardless of future development, heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding is expected in the region for the next couple of days.
In southeast Louisiana, rain drenched the area, with 3 to 6 inches falling in New Orleans overnight. Some areas could see up to 15 inches or more before the week is over.
New Orleans reported some damage from the rain and an early morning tornado while Jefferson Parish saw heavy flooding in cities like Kenner and Metairie.

First Alert: Tropical Moisture Keeps Rain and Storm Chances High Through Friday
Remnants of Tropical Storm Arthur bring heavy rain, a localized flooding threat, and a brief tornado risk to Alabama
MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - Warm, humid, and unsettled weather will continue across central and south Alabama through Friday as the remnants of Tropical Storm Arthur move inland and spread deep tropical moisture across the region. Numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected each day, with periods of heavy rain possible at times. The greatest concern will be localized flooding in areas that receive repeated rounds of rainfall. We will also be watching for the potential for a few brief, quick spin up tornadoes within heavier rain bands.
THURSDAY
Showers and thunderstorms will become numerous throughout the day as moisture associated with the remnants of Arthur overspreads the region. Rain may be heavy at times, especially during the afternoon and evening hours. Localized flooding will be possible where storms repeatedly move over the same locations. A few brief spin up tornadoes cannot be ruled out, particularly within heavier bands of rain. High temperatures will generally remain in the lower to middle 80s due to the increased cloud cover and rainfall.
THURSDAY NIGHT
Periods of showers and thunderstorms will continue through the night. Heavy rainfall may lead to additional localized flooding concerns, especially in low-lying and poor-drainage areas. The threat for a brief spin up tornado will continue as long as rain bands remain across the area. Lows will fall into the lower 70s.
Watch the latest live and local weather data below, streaming on WSFA Weather Now! Please note, this stream does not include live severe weather coverage, only data on the latest weather conditions.
FRIDAY
The remnants of Arthur continue to influence our weather, keeping rain and storm chances elevated. Numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected again, with heavy downpours remaining the primary threat. Additional localized flooding will be possible where rainfall accumulates the most. A brief tornado cannot be ruled out, although the overall threat remains low. Highs will remain in the lower to middle 80s.
THE WEEKEND
Rain chances begin to decrease, but scattered showers and thunderstorms will remain possible Saturday and Sunday. There will be more opportunities for dry weather compared to Thursday and Friday, although not everyone will stay completely dry. High temperatures will gradually warm back into the mid to upper 80s.
NEXT WEEK
A typical summertime pattern returns with warm and humid conditions. Scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms will remain possible each day, with highs climbing back toward 90 degrees.

Godo, riqualificato il tunnel di battuta dell’impianto sportivo Antonio Casadio dopo l’alluvione
All’impianto sportivo Antonio Casadio di Godo si chiude un nuovo capitolo di ricostruzione e rilancio, con la conclusione di un intervento di riqualificazione che ha trasformato il “tunnel di battuta” danneggiato dall’alluvione in una struttura autonoma e funzionale, collocata accanto agli spogliatoi e pensata per garantire maggiore sicurezza e continuità alle attività di baseball e softball.
L’inaugurazione si è svolta giovedì 18 giugno in via Rivalona 5, alla presenza della sindaca Valentina Palli, dell’assessore allo Sport Mirco Frega, di Livio Stellati, responsabile Sviluppo territoriale Region Centro Nord UniCredit, e dei rappresentanti delle società ASD Godo Baseball e AC Godo.
«L’inaugurazione di questa nuova struttura – spiega la sindaca Valentina Palli – rappresenta un momento particolarmente significativo per la nostra comunità. L’alluvione aveva colpito duramente questo impianto sportivo, mettendo in difficoltà società, atleti e famiglie che ogni giorno vivono questi spazi. Oggi, invece, siamo qui a celebrare un ulteriore risultato, dopo la straordinaria rete di solidarietà che, fin dai giorni dell’emergenza, ha visto impegnati enti, cittadini, volontari, realtà del territorio e non solo. Un ringraziamento particolare va a UniCredit, che ha scelto di sostenere questo progetto, contribuendo a riqualificare un luogo importante per l’aggregazione e la crescita dei nostri giovani. Questa struttura testimonia come, anche dopo eventi difficili, la collaborazione tra istituzioni, imprese e cittadini sia in grado di fare la differenza».
Sul valore strategico dell’intervento si è soffermato anche l’assessore allo Sport Mirco Frega: «Questo intervento – sottolinea – rappresenta un’opera strategica di potenziamento dell’impiantistica sportiva del territorio. La nuova struttura garantirà una maggiore fruibilità dell’impianto durante tutto l’anno, compresi i mesi autunnali e invernali, offrendo spazi adeguatamente protetti dalle intemperie. Oltre al tunnel di battuta, all’interno di tale spazio sarà allestita una palestra multifunzionale destinata agli atleti e alle attività giovanili delle società Baseball Godo e calcio AC Godo. Desidero ringraziare UniCredit per aver sostenuto con l’Amministrazione comunale questo investimento, che rappresenta non solo un intervento di riqualificazione sportiva, ma anche un’opportunità concreta per rafforzare le funzioni aggregative, educative e inclusive che lo sport svolge all’interno della comunità».
Per UniCredit è intervenuto Livio Stellati, responsabile Sviluppo territoriale Region Centro Nord: «Siamo davvero felici di aver contribuito a riqualificare il campo da baseball di Godo di Russi. Si tratta di uno dei progetti realizzati grazie a “Rigenerare”, un’iniziativa voluta da UniCredit che è stata, da subito e su più fronti, al fianco delle famiglie e delle imprese romagnole colpite dall’alluvione. Un aiuto concreto alla ricostruzione materiale dei luoghi, per restituire alle comunità spazi di incontro e di crescita. Con questo intervento confermiamo il nostro ruolo di partner affidabile e presente per il territorio, capace di ascoltarne le istanze e di far squadra con le istituzioni e la comunità per mettere a disposizione risorse in grado di favorire il benessere e la crescita dell’area e delle sue persone».
La riqualificazione del tunnel di battuta non rappresenta l’unico intervento completato nell’impianto sportivo di Godo. È infatti in fase di realizzazione una nuova cabina Enel che consentirà di alimentare le torri faro tramite un’utenza fissa, eliminando il generatore provvisorio precedentemente installato. Per quanto riguarda il calcio, dopo il recupero degli spogliatoi, delle panchine, delle porte da gioco e delle recinzioni perimetrali, sono previsti ulteriori interventi di completamento per risolvere le criticità funzionali ancora presenti. I lavori verranno eseguiti durante la pausa estiva delle attività sportive.
Fotoservizio di Gianni Zampaglione

Godo: The “batting tunnel” at the Antonio Casadio Sports Complex Has Been Renovated Following the Flood
A new chapter in the reconstruction and revitalization of the Antonio Casadio sports complex in Godo has come to a close with the completion of a renovation project that transformed the “batting tunnel”—damaged by the flood—into a self-contained and functional structure located next to the locker rooms and designed to ensure greater safety and continuity for baseball and softball activities.
The inauguration took place on Thursday, June 18, at Via Rivalona 5, in the presence of Mayor Valentina Palli, Councilor for Sports Mirco Frega, Livio Stellati, Head of Territorial Development for UniCredit’s Central-Northern Region, and representatives from the ASD Godo Baseball and AC Godo clubs.
“The inauguration of this new facility,” explains Mayor Valentina Palli, “represents a particularly significant moment for our community. The flood had severely damaged this sports complex, creating difficulties for the clubs, athletes, and families who use these spaces every day. Today, however, we are here to celebrate another achievement, following the extraordinary outpouring of solidarity that, ever since the emergency began, has involved local authorities, citizens, volunteers, community organizations, and others. Special thanks go to UniCredit, which chose to support this project, helping to revitalize an important place for our young people to come together and grow. This facility demonstrates how, even after difficult times, collaboration between institutions, businesses, and citizens can make a difference.”
Mirco Frega, Councilor for Sports, also highlighted the strategic value of the project: “This project,” he emphasized, “represents a strategic initiative to enhance the region’s sports infrastructure. The new facility will ensure greater year-round usability of the complex, including during the fall and winter months, by providing spaces adequately protected from the elements. In addition to the batting tunnel, this space will house a multifunctional gym for athletes and youth programs run by the Baseball Godo and AC Godo soccer clubs. “I would like to thank UniCredit for partnering with the municipal administration on this investment, which represents not only a sports redevelopment project but also a concrete opportunity to strengthen the social, educational, and inclusive roles that sports play within the community.”
Speaking on behalf of UniCredit was Livio Stellati, Head of Regional Development for the Central-Northern Region: “We are truly happy to have contributed to the redevelopment of the baseball field in Godo di Russi. This is one of the projects carried out thanks to ‘Rigenerare,’ an initiative launched by UniCredit that has stood by the families and businesses in Romagna affected by the flood from the very beginning and on multiple fronts. This is concrete support for the physical reconstruction of these areas, aimed at restoring spaces for community gathering and growth. With this project, we reaffirm our role as a reliable and committed partner for the region, capable of listening to its needs and teaming up with institutions and the community to provide resources that promote the well-being and growth of the area and its people.”
The renovation of the batting tunnel is not the only project completed at the Godo sports facility. In fact, a new Enel substation is currently under construction, which will allow the floodlight towers to be powered via a fixed utility connection, eliminating the need for the temporary generator previously installed. As for soccer, following the renovation of the locker rooms, benches, goals, and perimeter fencing, additional work is planned to address the remaining functional issues. The work will be carried out during the summer break from sports activities.
Photo essay by Gianni Zampaglione

Stonelick Township Fire & EMS crews started the morning off at 0215 for a tree down near the covered bridge on Stonelick Williams Corner Road. Two hours later during the torrential rains units were called again to Stonelick Williams Corner Road for a MVA with a person trapped in rising water and on the roof of their car. M-41 and E-41 were hampered by rising waters for the most direct route and had to take an alternate direction. 3 of the routes were inaccessible due to trees across the road, rising water or debris in the roadway.  Eventually M-40 was able to reach the occupant, get a safety rope to them and remove them from harm’s way.  While on scene, water kept rising stranding M-40s crew until the waters receded. 

While clearing that detail, crews were advised of a house that was completely surrounded by rushing water. Boats were requested from Central Joint Fire - EMS District and with the help of Williamsburg Township Emergency Services Chief 73, contact was made with the occupant and no further help was needed.  

Crews returned to service around 0800. We want to remind everyone to not drive through high water on roadways, rushing water doesn’t need to be very deep to carry objects downstream.

fact_alert.original_text:
Tunisie : des terres agricoles endommagées après la montée des eaux à Mellègue
Image d’illustration
La situation dans la zone de l’oued Mellègue reste sous contrôle, malgré la poursuite de l’écoulement des eaux consécutif à un incident technique survenu au niveau du barrage de Mellègue. Selon les autorités, des dégâts limités ont toutefois été enregistrés sur certaines terres agricoles.
D’après la Radio nationale, aucun danger n’est à signaler pour les habitants ou leurs biens, à l’exception de quelques parcelles agricoles situées en bordure de l’oued, notamment dans les zones d’El Aïn et El Maqla, qui ont été légèrement affectées.
Les autorités locales indiquent qu’un dispositif de vigilance renforcé a été mis en place, mobilisant la protection civile et la commission de lutte contre les catastrophes. Des équipes restent déployées sur le terrain afin de suivre l’évolution de la situation et d’intervenir en cas d’urgence.
Le barrage de Mellègue a également fait l’objet d’interventions techniques après la défaillance d’une vanne située sur la rive droite, ayant provoqué un important débit d’eau. Selon les responsables, les volumes évacués sont dirigés vers l’oued Medjerda, puis vers le barrage de Sidi Salem.
Le directeur général des barrages et des grands travaux hydrauliques au ministère de l’Agriculture a assuré que l’ouvrage reste sécurisé, précisant que l’incident constitue un cas inédit en Tunisie. Il a également indiqué que les travaux du barrage supérieur de Mellègue sont achevés et que sa mise en service est prévue pour l’automne prochain.
Dans un communiqué antérieur, la direction régionale de la protection civile de Jendouba avait appelé les riverains à la prudence et recommandé d’éviter les abords de l’oued, en raison de l’importante circulation des eaux.
S.R

fact_alert.translated_text:
Tunisia: Farmland Damaged After Flooding in Mellègue
Illustrative image
The situation in the Mellègue wadi area remains under control, despite continued water flow following a technical incident at the Mellègue dam. According to authorities, however, limited damage has been reported to some farmland.
According to National Radio, there is no danger to residents or their property, with the exception of a few agricultural plots located along the banks of the wadi—particularly in the El Aïn and El Maqla areas—which have been slightly affected.
Local authorities report that enhanced monitoring measures have been put in place, involving the civil defense and the disaster response commission. Teams remain deployed on the ground to monitor the situation and respond in case of an emergency.
The Mellègue Dam was also the subject of technical interventions following the failure of a gate on the right bank, which caused a significant flow of water. According to officials, the discharged water is being directed toward the Medjerda Wadi and then toward the Sidi Salem Dam.
The Director General of Dams and Major Hydraulic Works at the Ministry of Agriculture assured that the structure remains safe, noting that the incident is an unprecedented occurrence in Tunisia. He also indicated that work on the upper Mellègue Dam has been completed and that it is scheduled to become operational next fall.
In an earlier statement, the Jendouba Regional Civil Protection Directorate had urged local residents to exercise caution and recommended avoiding the area near the wadi due to the high water flow.
S.R

BALDWIN COUNTY, Ala. (WKRG) — As the remnants of Arthur make their way across the Gulf Coast, flooding is a threat.
The U.S. 90/98 Causeway has received water across the roadway, prompting the closure of eastbound traffic. ALGO cameras show officials diverting traffic exiting the Bankhead Tunnel onto the Bayway.
According to News 5 Meteorologist Caroline Carithers, the system is bringing heavy rain.
“Tropical moisture and instability are being pulled into the News 5 neighborhood, bringing rounds of torrential rain and thunderstorms, likely life-threatening flash flooding, some severe storms, and rough surf,” Carithers said.
Our viewing area is expecting 6-12 inches of rain with isolated spots possibly hitting 15 inches over the next two days.
That is creating a “particularly dangerous situation with life-threatening flooding“ today, according to the National Weather Service.
The NWS has also issued a rare level 4 out of 4 HIGH RISK for flash flooding for our area today.
The News 5 viewing area is under a Coastal Flood Advisory through 7 p.m. as coastal flooding is possible this afternoon during high tide, around 1 to 3 p.m. in the normal suspect spots, to include the U.S. 90/98 Causeway, Shell Belt and Coden Belt roads in Bayou La Batre, docks and boat ramps along Mobile Bay, and the Dauphin Island Causeway.
The News 5 First Alert Storm Team is tracking two kinds of flooding:
- Flash flooding is caused by heavy rainfall and high rainfall rates. Nearby Mississippi counties have received substantial rainfall, with 8-9 inches reported in Stone County.
- Coastal flooding is an issue because of “persistent southerly wind” and high water levels during high tide, expected between 1 and 3 p.m. today.
With any flooding, remember to avoid areas where the water covers the road.

Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WAIALUA (HawaiiNewsNow) - Amid the roaring, rushing sounds of heavy rain, those caught in the path of the historic Kona low floods in March were forced to abruptly flee their homes.
For the survivors, the terrifying sounds of that night will never leave them.
“All I could hear was metal screeching against one another, trees shaking, branches breaking, the rain falling, thunder,” recalled Kaleo Cyprian Valmoja-Galbiso, Otake Camp resident and flood survivor.
MORE: First Alert Hurricane Season 2026: Lessons from the Kona lows
At Otake Camp in Waialua, residents said facing a wall of water made survival nothing short of a miracle.
“All we could hear is each other’s screams and cries out of fear, because we didn’t know what was going to happen to us,” Valmoja-Galbiso said.
“When the water comes, it comes with force,” added Ryland Skaggs, Valmoja-Galbiso’s mother and Otake Camp resident.
“They’re trying to wake up people when this is happening, and you can imagine what these guys are going through. I got goose bumps telling you this,” said Marck Aphay, Otake Camp resident and flood survivor.
A night of rapid flooding and evacuation More than 5,500 North Shore residents were evacuated as the severely saturated ground simply couldn’t bear another drop.
Mount Kaala received a staggering 22 inches of rain, acting as a giant funnel that dumped high-velocity runoff directly into the basins below.
“It was 11:30 at night. We were already on flood watch due to the prior flooding that’s been happening,” Valmoja-Galbiso said.
Skaggs and her sons, Kaleo and Sage, have lived at Otake Camp for nearly 20 years. Her sons know the drill: watch the Kaukonahua Stream when heavy rains race down.
“Sage, he woke me up (and said) ‘Mom, the water level is at the berm.’ I told them both, we got to go now,” she recalled.
Over the rushing sounds of the swelling river, they scrambled into the dark to wake their most vulnerable neighbors.
“We walked out with whatever we had, whether some of us had shoes and others walked out barefoot,” Valmoja-Galbiso said.
“I told the boys, go back and go pound on the walls,” Skaggs said.
Evacuating required sheer physical willpower against the deluge.
“We had to dig our feet into the ground and pull ourselves against the current, and we had to carry the kids above our heads in their diapers and stay as a group as we exited. By that time, that is when the first responders showed up,” Valmoja-Galbiso said.
Floodwaters rise past 6 feet By the time help arrived, the raging flood waters had surpassed six feet, filling homes inside and out.
“At the peak of the flooding when we were evacuating everybody... I’m 5′11” and the water was up to my shoulders. So you can already tell, compared to my mom, she would have been completely submerged," Valmoja-Galbiso said.
The devastation at Otake Camp served as a reminder for the rest of Hawaii that disaster doesn’t always wait for sirens.
“Sirens didn’t go off here that night. But those first responders are so busy, I guarantee they had about a hundred million calls coming in,” Aphay said.
The scale of the disaster — and what was lost In a recent University of Hawai‘i study, researchers found that two trillion gallons of water flooded the islands during the event — enough to fill three million Olympic-sized swimming pools.
Three Otake Camp plantation houses were ripped from their foundations and carried down the river, displacing six families.
Aphay was working late when he got a frantic phone call from his brother.
“He said, ‘Hey, ours went down. Auntie Ry’s went down. Yours went down... Yours hit the bridge,’” Aphay said. “I said, ‘Nah, no way.’ ... He was just happy in my state to hear my voice, because I am alive.”
The water washed away decades of memories in a matter of minutes, survivors said.
Valmoja-Galbiso said, “At that point, we hit rock bottom, because all of our valuables, all of our mementos and our memories of our loved ones, our photos of childhoods, everything that we had went. We felt hollow.”
Gratitude amid the ruins Despite the destruction, survivors said they are grateful no lives were lost.
“You’re not thinking what to grab. You’re thinking who to grab,” Aphay said.
“We got everybody out safe,” Skaggs said.
“The final head count was a relief, but I still had that anxious pit in my stomach making sure,” Valmoja-Galbiso added.
Look closely at the earth where these homes once stood, and fragments of families’ lives still stick out of the mud: a warped ukulele, scattered crystals, old CDs. Inside one remaining structure, toys sit frozen in time, exactly where the receding waters dropped them.
The land holds memories built over decades — homes once filled with laughter and warmth from family gatherings, celebrations, and everyday life together.
Pointing to a blank space of dirt, Valmoja-Galbiso gestured, “This would be my backyard.”
Displaced residents adjust; volunteers step in For others, life has drastically downsized. Opening the doors of a repurposed food truck outfitted with a bed, Aphay shared his new reality.
“Basically, this is where I’m staying. So this bus was donated to me to use from Auntie Jen. I’ve been in here for about two months. This is enough for me right now,” Aphay said.
While living in the donated food truck, Aphay spends his days rebuilding what he can. American Red Cross signs are taped onto homes, marking the disaster zone and directing residents to aid. But residents said survival and relief often means relying on the community.
“Hawaii is very vulnerable to natural disasters and we just got to be proactive,” said volunteer Cody Silver. “The people that got proactive and started buying their own material... They’re the ones that are actually living back in their homes now.”
Even with daunting obstacles, volunteers continue to arrive. Tuan Nguyen suffered a broken arm when his ladder collapsed while replacing shingles on a damaged roof in the camp. Despite the injury, he keeps showing up.
“Just the love and support from community, it drives me to still be out here to help people,” Nguyen said.
“If we work together, the process goes by a lot faster,” Aphay said.
Preparing for what could come next For Otake Camp survivors, preparedness is no longer a seasonal chore — it is a daily reality, especially as shifting climate patterns threaten longer, more active hurricane seasons.
John Bravender with the National Weather Service Honolulu warned, “The weather system that we saw back in March and April, especially the large Kona low, had a lot of wind and a lot of rain. A hurricane will be very similar to that, even more intense.”
Hurricanes are fueled by warm seas and can bring even more violent destruction.
“This is something small compared to a hurricane I can only imagine, so we got to look out for each other and remind each other, remember what happened last time?” Aphay said.
“Don’t think that it is not going to happen to you. Always be prepared for when it does,” Valmoja-Galbiso urged.
“Always look at your surroundings. If you live next to a river like we did, we always watch the river,” Skaggs said.
‘Don’t forget about Otake Camp’ Today, the rebuilding process is fueled by tearful embraces and shared resilience among victims and the volunteers helping them heal.
“You’re a big part of my life, you know,” Aphay told one of his supporters, known as Auntie Jen, during an emotional group hug.
“Don’t forget about Otake Camp,” she said.
“Not everybody’s fortunate to have somebody in their lives like that,” Valmoja-Galbiso said. “So be that person for the next.”

Families escape by boat as floodwaters devastate Stone County RV Park
STONE COUNTY, Miss. (WDAM) - Thursday, families at Perk Beach RV Park escaped rising floodwaters that overtook the property after heavy rainfall moved through south Mississippi.
Some residents waded through waist-deep water to reach safety, while others were evacuated by boat as floodwaters surrounded homes, vehicles, and roadways throughout the park.
For resident Chrissy Martin, the flooding unfolded quickly.
“I woke up, and the water was getting pretty high, and I had to figure out what to do,” Martin said.
Although Martin was able to get out safely, she said much of what she owns remains trapped in the floodwaters.
“My whole life’s in there, everything I own,” she said. “My car’s in there. I drive for a living. I do non-emergency medical transport, so that’s all that I have in there. It’s my life. My car is my life. That’s how I pay my bills.”
Resident Debra-Lynn Sloan said they’ve weathered heavy rain before, but describes this flooding event as unlike anything she’s seen before.
“When we get a lot of rain, the creek will come up, but it’s never come this high, but it just kept coming, and there’s nowhere for the water to go,” Sloan said.
As conditions worsened, residents gathered pets and whatever belongings they could carry before leaving the park.
Sloan said one of her biggest concerns is the lack of shelter options that accommodate pets.
“I got my 13-year-old little beagle out; she’s in my car,” Sloan said. “There’s a shelter in Wiggins at the community center, but you’re not allowed to bring your dog or your cat. They are saying that they will take the dogs someplace else, but folks are not going to want to leave their animals.”
The flooding affected more than just residents. A small kitten was rescued from the floodwaters, providing a brief moment of hope during a day filled with uncertainty.
RELATED: Kitten rescued from floodwaters by Perkinston RV park manager, residents
As the water slowly recedes, many residents are now facing the reality of what comes next.
“It’s not even hard yet; it has to resonate,” Martin said. “I haven’t even grasped it. I have nowhere to go. So I’m homeless, and on the streets now, I haven’t even comprehended that yet.”
Residents said their most immediate needs include temporary housing, pet-friendly shelter options, and assistance replacing essential items lost in the flooding.

Highways 49 and 26 in Stone County heavily impacted by severe flooding
STONE COUNTY, Miss. (WXXV)- Dangerous conditions on some of Stone County’s major highways continue this evening.
Many streets in Wiggins became impassable Thursday morning as the rain moved through.
In Perkinston, Highway 49 at Red Creek was closed in both directions as water came up to the tops of the bridges there, but MHP officials tell us both directions are back open this evening.
As water came up to the top of the bridge and similar situations played out along Highway 26 East in the White’s Crossing community. Stone County Sheriff Todd Stewart said, “Well it’s been a hot mess since we been getting all of that weather. We’ve had trees down; we got roads still flooded. We still got nine emergency calls waiting to be rescued via boat but thank God we have help from neighbors. As far as the community, Jackson County, we got help from up north so we’re just very thankful but we still got people trapped in their houses. Roads that are closed due to flooding. So, we’re slowly but surely trying to get everybody rescued that needs to be rescued. We probably will get another band of rain talking with the EMA director, we’re probably going to have another band of rain. So, I would just advise everyone to stay in-place if there’s no need to get out, do not get out on the roadways because if you’re out on the roadways and you run into a road closure, you’re doing nothing but hampering the first responders that are out here trying to get people out the homes and rescue them.”

fact_alert.original_text:
Importante notizia per gli amanti della natura. La strada era stata messa fuori uso dopo l’alluvione del maggio 2023
Ricevi le notizie de il Resto del Carlino su Google Seguici In quest’inizio estate una buona notizia per gli amanti della natura e per i residenti: torna finalmente raggiungibile la frazione di Ville di Montiego e con essa l’accesso al monte, un paradiso per gli amanti di trekking, bike e arrampicata. Dopo l’alluvione del maggio 2023 che aveva portato precipitazioni eccezionali aggravando la situazione di dissesto idrogeologico, infatti, la frazione più lontana del comune di Urbania, che sorge sul versante est del Montiego a 660 metri di altitudine, era rimasta isolata da dei grandi fronti di frana che avevano interessato l’unica strada che raggiunge l’abitato.
Un primo pronto intervento della Regione aveva permesso il transito in modo provvisorio ma per stabilizzare la situazione si è acceduti a questo importante finanziamento di 2 milioni di euro per intervenire in modo definitivo. L’ intervento, ormai in fase di ultimazione, ha previsto il ripristino della viabilità in armonia al tracciato preesistente, attraverso dei lavori di riprofilatura delle scarpate con realizzazione di un rafforzamento con reti metalliche accoppiate a materiali geocompositi. Le maestranze sul posto hanno lavorato anche al rimodellamento dei sedimenti esistenti al fine di migliorare la pendenza del tracciato, hanno creato una corretta regimazione delle acque ed è stato anche necessario rimuovere i massi pericolanti ed instabili. Sono poi state installate delle reti paramassi nella sommità dell’area di frana, al fine di rendere definitivo ed accessibile in completa sicurezza il tracciato stradale che conduce all’abitato di Montiego.
La progettazione e direzione lavori è stata affidata allo studio Paci srl di Pesaro e la realizzazione dell’intervento è stata aggiudicata alla ditta Dinamicgeo srl di Mezzolombardo in provincia di Trento. La notizia farà felici gli amanti dello sport all’aria aperta che da lì raggiungono pareti di arrampicata iconiche come Balza della Penna o sentieri per trekking e bici segnalati e tra i più belli del territorio.
"Non solo rivolgiamo molta attenzione al capoluogo – ha commentato il sindaco Marco Ciccolini –, ma programmiamo interventi anche sulle frazioni e in tutto il territorio comunale, anche quello più lontano, con investimenti importanti. Ville di Montiego non ha cittadini residenti fissi ma ha una comunità vivace e brillante che si ritrova ogni estate ed è spesso meta di campi estivi oltre che di amanti dell’outdoor. Con questi lavori sarà fruibile in piena sicurezza".
Andrea Angelini

fact_alert.translated_text:
Important news for nature lovers. The road had been closed following the May 2023 flood
Get news from *Il Resto del Carlino* on Google. Follow us. As summer begins, here’s some good news for nature lovers and residents: the hamlet of Ville di Montiego is finally accessible again, and with it, access to the mountain—a paradise for hikers, cyclists, and climbers. Following the May 2023 flood—which brought exceptional rainfall and exacerbated the hydrogeological instability—the most remote hamlet in the municipality of Urbania, situated on the eastern slope of Montiego at an elevation of 660 meters, had been cut off by large landslides that had blocked the only road leading to the settlement.
An initial emergency response by the Region had allowed temporary access, but to stabilize the situation, this significant funding of 2 million euros was secured to implement a permanent solution. The project, now nearing completion, involved restoring road access in accordance with the existing route by reprofiling the slopes and reinforcing them with metal mesh combined with geocomposite materials. Workers on site also reshaped the existing sediment to improve the road’s gradient, established proper water management, and removed unstable and hazardous boulders. Rockfall protection nets were then installed at the top of the landslide area to ensure the road leading to the town of Montiego is permanently safe and fully accessible.
The design and construction supervision were entrusted to the firm Paci srl of Pesaro, and the contract for the project was awarded to Dinamicgeo srl of Mezzolombardo in the province of Trento. The news will delight outdoor sports enthusiasts who use this route to reach iconic climbing walls such as Balza della Penna or well-marked hiking and biking trails—among the most beautiful in the region.
“Not only do we pay close attention to the town center,” commented Mayor Marco Ciccolini, “but we also plan projects for the outlying villages and throughout the entire municipal territory—even the most remote areas—with significant investments.” Ville di Montiego has no permanent residents but boasts a lively and vibrant community that gathers there every summer; it is often a destination for summer camps as well as for outdoor enthusiasts. With these improvements, the area will be fully accessible in complete safety.”

Water Service Cut Off in 20 Settlements in the Stavropol Region Due to Flooding
In the Stavropol Region, due to flooding and murky water, the water supply from the water treatment plants in the village of Kursavka and the town of Kaskadny has been reduced by 30%. This was reported by "Stavropolkrayvodokanal."
Photo: Yegor Snetkov, Kommersant
As specified in the announcement, there will be no drinking water for 10 days in the Andropov District. "The reason is the inflow of floodwaters, which causes the turbidity of the raw water to remain as high as 160 mg/L, requiring a longer treatment and settling process," the statement said.
Currently, there is no water supply in twenty settlements, namely Kursavka, Surkul, Krymgireevskoye, Sultan, Verkhniy Kalaus, Kurshava, Nikolaevsky, Kunakovsky, Soluno-Dmitrievskoye, Alekseevskoye, Krasnoyarskoye, Vorovskoleskaya, Vodrazdel, Dubovaya Balka, Kiankiz, Yankul, Novy Yankul, Nizhnekolonsky, Verkhny Yankul, Ovrazhny, Kaskadny, Podgorny, and Kazinka in the Andropov District, as well as the village of Ulyanovka in the Mineralnye Vody District.

Flooding Remains the Main Concern as Heavy Rain Continues
Ashlyn’s Forecast
COLUMBUS, Ga. (WTVM) - The severe weather threat for tonight has come to an end, but the next focus will be the potential for flooding in some areas. A Flood Watch remains in effect through Friday.
Periods of heavy rain will continue through tonight. Widespread rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches are expected, with locally higher amounts of 5 inches or more possible. A few non-severe thunderstorms with gusty winds may still occur, but for most of us, it will simply be a steady soaking rain overnight.
Some heavy rain will linger into Friday morning, mainly across our southern communities. This is where the flooding threat appears to be highest. A few typical afternoon pop-up showers and thunderstorms are also expected Friday, but they will not be nearly as widespread as what we saw today. However, it’s important to note that any additional rainfall could worsen flooding in areas that have already received significant rain.
Looking ahead, we return to a more typical summertime pattern with scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms over the next several days. By Father’s Day, highs will climb into the upper 80s. Next week, temperatures in the low 90s are expected to return, especially on days that trend a bit drier, such as Monday and Friday.

Friday

Hydrological Warning No. 39

In regulated watersheds, warning levels may be exceeded in the event of particularly heavy rainfall.

fact_alert.original_text:
Pearl River County braces for third flood event in four days
PEARL RIVER COUNTY, Miss. (WLOX) — Already battered by Tuesday’s flooding, Pearl River County was slammed by the remnants of Arthur.
Homes, businesses and infrastructure are left damaged while record flooding is on the horizon.
In a county already rocked by flood damage, the remnants of Arthur are not making things any easier for people like Sean and Kaylee Kennedy.
They inherited their house after their parents passed away a year ago.
“Tuesday, it flood big for the first time. We had to rip out the carpet, and then, today, I guess from ripping out the carpet, it spread really quickly throughout the house, and we thought the sandbags would help but they didn’t,” Sean Kennedy said.
Their story is echoed by homeowners across the county.
Arthur put people and homes in danger and also infrastructure.
Unprecedented overflow at the Anchor Lake dam put it at risk of failure.
“I’ve never seen it like this before. I’ve seen it go over the road, but not impassable,” Michelle Dunn said.
Although Dunn’s home is not directly at risk, volunteer firefighters and sheriff deputies went door to door to her neighbors, urging people to leave.
Unprecedented river flooding is on its way, with both the East and West Hobolochitto expected to crest over 22 feet.
For the third time in just four days, the county is bracing for impact.
